design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (excess_flood_layering, env_0065).

[0] Draw (draw_counts.py ... --task 1): {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Prerequisite excess_ext_loss_of_use_payment takes 6 factors, root excess_ext_sale_cancellation_return takes 5.

[1] Why this is a good test. Diane Sutherland asks only to cancel the excess policy on the Isle of Palms house she sold and get the premium owed back. The agent must notice in the cancellation rule that the returned premium is not fixed until every claim whose latest adjuster report documents more loss of use than has been paid carries a loss-of-use payment issued after that report; find in the claim file that the SUPPLEMENTAL report of 2026-09-04 (103,640) postdates the last loss-of-use payment (2026-06-12, total 31,970); work out from the loss-of-use rule that issuing that payment is the one write that brings the state about; figure the payment with six adjustments read from the claim's own entries and the underlying HomeFlood records (old home sold, underlying tier); and only then figure the returned premium with five adjustments, one of which (the loss-of-use charge retention) moves because of the payment. The rows reconciled: 12 excess claim rows, 20 premium rows, 3 servicing rows, 2 HomeFlood policies with their request, 10 claim rows, 23 premium rows and 6 servicing documents.

[2] Scope snapshot. Occupied by task 0: excess_ext_renewal_term_premium, excess_ext_limit_increase_premium and their tools. Claimed by task 1: excess_ext_loss_of_use_payment (pay_excess_loss_of_use_f5cb8480, agent) and excess_ext_sale_cancellation_return (sign_excess_sale_cancellation_a26754a5, user). Together the two tasks cover all four extended policies; scopes disjoint.

[3] Problem-tree card. Root P_CAN (owner=user). Edge P_CAN -> P_LOU, kind value_input, gate retention_share, form state. Prerequisite sentence (negated direction, as a refund desk says a refund is not fixed until claims are paid up): "The returned premium on a sale cancellation is not fixed until every claim on the policy whose latest adjuster report documents more loss of use than has been paid carries a loss-of-use payment issued after that report." Four-point test: connective "not ... until"; waits on a record-visible state (a LOSS_OF_USE payment row dated after the latest report); names no tool, id or code token; scoped to claims whose latest report exceeds payments. Only the loss-of-use payment tool writes a loss-of-use payment row in this difficulty. Opening falsity: excess_claims s3 (2026-09-04, 103,640) vs latest LOSS_OF_USE payment 2026-06-12. Order [P_LOU, P_CAN]. Deletion sensitivity: without the payment the returned premium recomputes to 1,669.79 (retention half) instead of 1,588.38. The charter now states prerequisite sentences in both directions (task 0 affirmative "only once", task 1 negated "not ... until").

[4] Base-invariant card. Step 12 (excess_claim_paid): excess_claim_settlement (policy_scope) — payable less net prior payments, positive only, to the insured; its first-dollar loss-of-use sentence retired by declared overwrite for loss-of-use payments under this rule. Step 14 (excess_policy_cancelled): excess_cancellation_refund — its gate sentence (signed request on file, status pending_effective/active) retired for sale cancellations by declared overwrite whose replaced_by keeps the status condition and makes the signature given with the cancellation the signed request; the PROPERTY_SOLD effective-date clause and the pro rata/minimum clause retired the same way; the paid-claim bar stays in force (date of loss 2025-10-03 is before the 2026-07-01 term). No time gate applies (pol_deadline governs proof-of-loss receipt only).

[5] Business-object card. Policy EXF-4472019 on 456 Palm Blvd; claim XC-4310887 (underlying claim HFC-4402173). Loss-of-use payment rows of XC-4310887 enter the netting; the 265,000 building payment is excluded by coverage. The HomeFlood offset reads only the tier of the HomeFlood policy named as the underlying (HFL-4825561); the HomeFlood claim file is seeded for realism and read in gold, but no computation reads it. Cancellation object: the 2026-07-01 term; the credits and refund reference the request the tool writes.

[6] Factor card — loss-of-use payment (6). The claim is the one carrying the latest adjuster report; every claim read is filtered to it. baseline: latest incurred 103,640 capped at 100,000, less 31,970 issued = 68,030.00, plus 8% interest for 230 days after the base due date (2026-02-27) = 71,459.46. comparable_housing_share param (0.304% of RCV per month -> 90%; baseline 22,077.17); displacement_period_end method, multi-source (HomeFlood cancelled for sale 2026-08-28 before the report -> 329/336; baseline 13,847.61); primary_lou_offset method, cross-difficulty homeflood (the underlying policy number is the Tidemark HomeFlood Premier policy -> its tier loss-of-use limit 50,000 is subtracted, the layer never paying inside the primary's cover; another carrier's primary would take 10% of the underlying dwelling limit, an NFIP primary nothing; baseline 62,049.19); loss_severity_allowance param (FINAL whole dwelling loss 40.8% of RCV -> 2,500 moving and storage allowance inside the payable, netted against the 2,500 already issued 2025-12-04; baseline 9,390.97); interest_due_anchor method (SUPPLEMENTAL -> due 2026-10-04, 11 days; baseline due date 2026-02-27 under the base sentence, 230 days; declared override with the base content restated for other payments; baseline 12,610.27); claim_age_rate param (12 whole months -> 10%; baseline 8%: 11,891.35). Result 11,898.50.

[7] Factor card — returned premium (5). baseline: earned to the closing (58 days), 25% minimum -> min(2323.10 x 307/365, 1742.33) = 1,742.32 (as recomputed). backdating_limit method (request 48 days after the closing -> effective 2026-09-15, 76 earned days; baseline 1,692.58); unexpired_cutoff method, cross-difficulty (declarations expire 2027-06-25 -> 6 days removed; baseline 1,623.11); tenure_minimum_waiver param, multi-source (4 renewals AND layer payments in the last 12 months -> 10%, cap not reached; baseline 25% binds: 1,529.50); use_charge_retention param (latest loss-of-use payment on/after term start -> whole; baseline 1,751.20); early_cancellation_charge param (closing 58 days into the term -> 50; baseline 1,638.38). Result 1,588.38; tool adds 95.30 tax credit and refunds 1,683.68.

[8] Factor independence. claim_in_hand, underlying_claim_no, sale_closing, date_of_loss, report_date, report_incurred, displacement_months, prior_lou_paid, term_days are plain shared bindings stated once in the rules; no factor binding reads another factor's binding; assembly in lou_payable/lou_due/late_interest/result and unexpired_days/returned_core/lou_retained/result.

[9] Method tier pairwise table. displacement_period_end: sale vs months-cap differ by a HomeFlood cancellation for sale; months-cap vs as-reported differ by displacement months > tier maximum; sale vs as-reported differ by the sale record. primary_lou_offset: HomeFlood-limit vs other-carrier share differ by whether the underlying policy number is a Tidemark HomeFlood record (different source and formula); other-carrier share vs none differ by underlying type (private vs NFIP); HomeFlood-limit vs none by the HomeFlood record of the underlying number. interest_due_anchor: supplemental vs final-with-proof by report type; final-with-proof vs base due date by a loss-of-use proof on file; supplemental vs base due date by report type. backdating_limit: 31-90 vs >90 vs <=30 days after closing. unexpired_cutoff: declarations-expiry vs HomeFlood-record-end differ by the declarations date; HomeFlood-record vs none by the HomeFlood term end.

[10] Edge probes. No HomeFlood record: sale_closing None -> period stands as reported, offset 0 (first dollar); offset limit and HomeFlood term end read the record of the underlying policy number (a second HomeFlood row at the address is not read); the offset never depends on what the HomeFlood claim file shows paid; a second excess claim does not enter the reads (filtered to the claim carrying the latest report); no FINAL report -> severity 0; underlying policy number not a HomeFlood record and the underlying private -> 10% of the underlying dwelling limit; NFIP underlying -> no offset; no loss-of-use payment ever -> retention nothing; latest report FINAL with no loss-of-use proof -> base due date (later of latest proof and underlying settlement), none where neither is on file; displacement months 0 -> counted as one (no division by zero); paid claim with a date of loss in the term -> nothing returned.

[11] Persona. Brisk administrator; volunteers sale, closing date context and the cancellation request; signs herself; identity on request; the claim and the September report only when asked; accepts a living-expense payment if the agent says one is due; ends after the cancellation and refund are confirmed.

[12] Standard solution and verification. Reads as in evaluation_criteria; pay 11,898.50 on XC-4310887; hand over the cancellation: effective 2026-09-15, returned premium 1,588.38. Harness (replays gold with the real tools, evaluates through check_compute): loss-of-use 11898.5 with {22077.17, 13847.61, 62049.19, 9390.97, 12610.27, 11891.35, all-baseline 71459.46}; returned premium 1588.38 with {1692.58, 1623.11, 1529.5, 1751.2, 1638.38, all-baseline 1742.32}; returned premium without the payment 1669.79.

[13] Revisions. HomeFlood old-home term moved to 2026-06-25..2027-06-25 so that the 25% minimum binds in the minimum-waiver baseline (first draft left that factor decorative); an earning-period split for a mid-term decrease was dropped because pro rata earning makes it identical to the single-period figure; a cancellation-date anchor factor was dropped because base already fixes the closing date for sales (a fall-through to the receipt date would be a straw man), replaced by the backdating limit.

REWORK round 2: relocation allowance replaced by a severity-based moving and storage allowance inside the payable (history re-derived: a 2,500 item on 2025-12-04 after the FINAL report); offset no longer lets the layer drop down (below-limit tier subtracts the HomeFlood limit) and reads only the underlying claim and the underlying policy number; all claim reads confined to the claim carrying the latest report; due-date override of the base intake sentence declared; minimum-earned waiver re-keyed to renewals and layer payments in 12 months; paid-claim bar netted for voids and declared; the 2026-07-01 renewal premium re-derived under the revised loss-history ladder (2323.10); contents attachment set to 250,000; FINAL report and building proof of loss moved inside the 60-day window.
REWORK round 3: the underlying offset ladder now has three distinct methods reachable on charter-producible worlds (Tidemark HomeFlood underlying -> its tier limit; another carrier's private primary -> 10 percent of the underlying dwelling limit; NFIP -> first dollar); the HomeFlood claim-file read was dropped from the gold reads (no decision rests on it), shifting the write steps to 8 and 10.
REWORK round 4 (renderer source scan): late-payment interest now has a standard method in the computation (8 percent a year from the base due date), so the due-date anchor and the claim-age rate each change the result on their own; displacement cut states whole displacement months and a sale on or after the loss; every overwrite tail restates the base content it keeps; same-day tie-break stated; single-factor bindings moved into their factors. Scored values unchanged.
REWORK round 5: the interest due-date sentence no longer carries the undefined 'documented on a later report' qualifier (the tiers read the latest adjuster report's kind directly); report kind and displacement months moved into their factors; tie-break sentence covers two policy records answering the same description (first entered read). Adversarial probes (second claim, voids on another claim, expired HomeFlood entered first, fully voided current-term claim) leave both figures unchanged. Scored values unchanged.
REWORK round 6: every read a second record of the same kind could answer is now keyed by its identifying value: the sale closing date and the unexpired-day cut read the Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose number is the underlying policy number on the policy record (HFL-4825561), the underlying declarations are read for that underlying number, every claim read is keyed by the claim of the latest adjuster report, and the FINAL report, the loss-of-use proof of loss and the settlement record are each the latest of their kind. Decoy probes (a second HomeFlood policy on the same address cancelled for a sale on another date, later declarations for another underlying number) leave both results unchanged; no scored value moved.
REWORK round 10 (seed only; charter and tools byte-identical): the HomeFlood records now carry what the published HomeFlood rules write. HFL-4825561 (Premier, AE, 1,000,000/250,000, deductible 5,000, certificate +3 ft received with the application of 2021-06-11, 14-day standard wait to 2021-06-25): term premiums on the rate manual (6,425 of rate amounts x zone 1.0 x elevation 0.45 x deductible 0.85, less credits, plus the 160 loss-of-use charge) - 2,617.56 for 2021 and 2022 (no credit), 2,494.68 for 2023 (package 5), 2,371.81 for 2024 and 2025 (package 5 + claims-free 5), 2,494.68 for 2026 (package only; the 2025-10-03 paid loss removes claims-free), each renewal offered 60 days before the term end and booked at the offer with no renewal adjustment (check payments five days ahead, under 60 months insured, no NFIP line, no nonpayment notices), policy fee 35 each term. Cancellation: the signed property-sold request with the settlement statement, effective 2026-08-28, processed 2026-09-03; the credit under the current HomeFlood cancellation credit rule is pro rata on the sale but the paid-claim share is nothing (1,230,000 paid on the 2025-10-03 loss, at least 25 percent of 1,250,000 of limits, inside 12 months), no exit fee (62 months in force) and half the policy fee back (64 days into the term, 9 months left): 17.50, credited to the term premium item and refunded to the insured. Claim HFC-4402173: actual cash value settlement (1,000,000 is below 80 percent of 3,100,000), dwelling 1,086,400 less the 5,000 deductible capped at the 1,000,000 limit, personal property 180,000 at replacement cost, loss of use 28,400 then 21,600 up to the 50,000 Premier limit within 12 months; the excess settlement record now shows the 1,000,000 the underlying paid. HFL-4917380 (Plus, zone X, 600,000/150,000, deductible 2,500): new business 1,263.86 plus the 35 fee paid by escrow on the 2026-08-20 application. Gold reads of the HomeFlood requests, claims, billing and servicing documents (steps 7-10) cover the new rows, shifting the writes to steps 12 and 14. No compute reads these rows; no scored value moved.
user_scenario:
You are Diane Sutherland, a brisk, organized hospital administrator in her fifties who has had a long year. Tidemark insured your old house at 456 Palm Blvd, Isle of Palms, SC 29451 with a HomeFlood policy and an Excess Flood policy above it. A flood badly damaged that house in October 2025, your family has been living in a rental since, and rather than rebuild you sold the house as it stood; the sale closed on August 28, 2026, the same day you closed on your new home at 447 Coleman Blvd in Mount Pleasant. The HomeFlood policy on the old house was already cancelled at the closing. You are calling now to cancel the Excess Flood policy on the old house because you sold it, and to get back whatever premium is owed to you; you want the cancellation done on this call and you will sign it yourself. You are not asking about anything else.

You give your details only when the agent asks: your phone number is 8435547719 and the last four of your Social Security number are 4682. If a further detail is needed, your ZIP code is 29464 and your email is diane.sutherland@gmail.com. You don't have policy or claim numbers handy and ask the agent to look them up. If the agent asks for the closing date, you say August 28, 2026, and that you have the settlement statement if they need it. If the agent asks why you are calling only now, you say the move took over your life for a few weeks.

Only if the agent asks: yes, there was a claim on the old house after the October 2025 flood; the building part was paid long ago and the excess policy has also been paying your temporary rent; the adjuster sent another living-expense report in early September and you have not seen anything since. If the agent says a living-expense payment is due to you and will be issued, you say thank you, that's welcome, and you don't ask how it is worked out. You don't know how cancellation refunds are calculated and you don't suggest any figures.

When the agent tells you the cancellation date and the premium you will get back, you accept it as explained. When the agent hands you the cancellation to sign, you sign it using exactly the date and amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation if asked. Once the agent tells you the cancellation and refund are done, you thank them and end the call. If the agent says the cancellation cannot be done, you ask for the reason in one sentence, thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: For every excess claim of the policy whose latest excess_adjuster_report shows loss_of_use_incurred above the loss-of-use payments issued, an excess_claim_paid row with coverage_part LOSS_OF_USE dated after that report stands on excess_claims.
edges.policy_source: The returned premium on a sale cancellation is not fixed until every claim on the policy whose latest adjuster report documents more loss of use than has been paid carries a loss-of-use payment issued after that report.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Claim XC-4310887's latest report (SUPPLEMENTAL 2026-09-04) documents 103,640 of loss of use while the loss-of-use payments issued total 31,970, the latest on 2026-06-12, before the report.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The payment of 11,898.50 dated 2026-10-15 stands on the claim after the 2026-09-04 report; the latest loss-of-use payment then falls on or after the 2026-07-01 term start and the retention share moves from half to whole.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One edge; nothing else is reordered. Signing the cancellation first would fix the returned premium at 1,669.79 with the retention at half, and the loss-of-use payment issued afterwards would leave a different terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the loss-of-use payment leaves the latest loss-of-use payment at 2026-06-12, the retention at half (81.41 instead of 162.82) and the returned premium at 1,669.79 instead of 1,588.38; the claim file also lacks the 11,898.50 payment.
